title: The Relief Share on Interest in a Dispute Rebill
content:
Interest the cardholder should not bear while a dispute was open is relieved from the rebill on a card under Personal Credit Cards, and the relief share is read from the age of the card account and from whether it has been rebilled before.

*Where the card account has been open at least 48 whole months and no earlier dispute rebill has been posted to it*, the relief share on interest is 100 percent.

*Where the card account has been open at least 48 whole months and at least one earlier dispute rebill has been posted to it*, the relief share on interest is 50 percent.

*Where the card account has been open less than 48 whole months*, no relief share is applied to the interest.

**What each tier is worth.** On a hypothetical interest figure of 41.50 USD, the first tier relieves 41.50 USD, the second relieves 20.75 USD and the third relieves nothing.

**On the boundaries.** The age of the account is read as at least, so an account open exactly 48 whole months falls in one of the first two tiers and one open 47 whole months in the third, whatever its rebill history. Between the first two tiers the count separates at none against one or more: a card account carrying a single earlier dispute rebill takes 50 percent, and one carrying no earlier rebill at all takes 100 percent.
